title: Why Did the FBI Show Up at Reporters’ Doors?
summary: Picture this: You’re a reporter, and you’ve just written a big story about the president’s airplane. Then, on a Friday night, there’s a knock at your door—it’s the FBI, and they hand you a subpoena. That means you have to go to court and answer questions. That’s what happened to four journalists from The New York Times. Their articles said that the Secret Service told President Trump to use an older Air Force One jet because the new one, a gift from Qatar, was missing important safety features like antimissile defenses. The stories used unnamed sources—people who shared secret information. The government says it’s not after the reporters; it just wants to find the leakers. But many are worried. A lawyer for the Times said it should “shock the conscience” of anyone who cares about press freedom. Another group called it part of a “war on the press.” Earlier this year, the FBI even searched another reporter’s home and took her phones and laptops. The president has often called the media “the enemy.” Critics say these moves are meant to scare journalists so they stop investigating the government. The reporters haven’t revealed their sources, and the case is still going on.
why_it_matters: This story shows that even though reporters have a right to share important information, they can face serious legal pressure, which might stop them from doing their job of keeping the public informed.

background_read: Air Force One is not just one plane; it is the call sign for any Air Force aircraft carrying the president. A new version is being built, but the older model is still in use. Qatar is a small but wealthy country in the Middle East.

The Secret Service is in charge of keeping the president safe, so they must check any plane for dangers. Antimissile defenses are systems that protect a plane from missiles fired at it. Without them, the president could be at risk.
Article_Structure: WHO: Four journalists from The New York Times.
WHAT: They received subpoenas after reporting that the Secret Service warned President Trump about missing antimissile defenses on a new Air Force One jet gifted by Qatar.
WHERE: The FBI delivered the subpoenas to the reporters’ homes on a Friday night.
WHY: The government wants to force the reporters to reveal the unnamed sources who leaked the secret safety information.

perspectives.description: They believe the subpoenas are an attack on a free press and are meant to silence reporters who investigate the government.
They argue that leaks about the president’s airplane could put lives in danger, so finding the leakers is a top priority.
They worry that the public deserves to know if the president’s plane lacks vital protections, and that the reporters did the right thing by exposing the risk.
